new.title: Feel the Yellow Wall at Signal Iduna Park
new.desc: Borussia Dortmund's home ground holds about 81,000 spectators and is the largest football stadium in Germany. Its south stand, the Südtribüne, is Europe's biggest standing terrace with some 25,000 places.
new.tip: Stadium tours of about 90 minutes run on non-match days and take in the tunnel and dressing rooms; book ahead.

new.title: Explore the German Football Museum
new.desc: The national football museum of the German FA opened in 2015 opposite Dortmund's main station. Exhibits run from the 1954 World Cup win to the present, with trophies, shirts and interactive stations.
new.tip: Allow two to three hours and book online. The Dortmunder U is a short walk away.
new.q: Deutsches Fußballmuseum, Platz der Deutschen Einheit 1, Dortmund

new.title: Tour Zeche Zollern, the palace of work
new.desc: Zeche Zollern II/IV in Bövinghausen was built from 1898 as a showcase colliery and is now an LWL industrial museum. Its machine hall has a Jugendstil entrance portal and is one of the best-known industrial monuments in the Ruhr.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays. Take a guided tour to see the pit baths and the winding towers.
new.q: LWL-Industriemuseum Zeche Zollern, Grubenweg 5, Bövinghausen, Dortmund

new.title: Walk the Kokerei Hansa coking plant
new.desc: The Kokerei Hansa in Huckarde was a coking plant built in 1927-28 and closed in 1992, and is a protected industrial monument. Visitors walk through the coal tower, pipe corridors and machine house.
new.tip: Guided tours and a trail exist; check the Industriedenkmalstiftung page for current opening days.

new.title: Circle the Phoenix-See lake in Hörde
new.desc: The Phoenix-See is a 24-hectare artificial lake built on the former Phoenix-Ost steelworks site and opened in 2011. A loop path of about 3 km runs around it, with a harbour, restaurants and rental boats in season.
new.tip: Walk the loop at sunset; pedal and rowing boats are rented in the warmer months.

new.title: Take in art and views at the Dortmunder U
new.desc: The Dortmunder U is the former Union brewery's tower, now a cultural centre with the Museum Ostwall and a gold-lit U on top. A roof terrace gives a view over the city.
new.tip: Check opening times for the museum; the U lights up at night and is best seen from the Hauptbahnhof side.

new.title: Ride up the Florianturm in Westfalenpark
new.desc: The Florianturm, 220 metres high, was Germany's tallest telecommunications tower when built in 1959 and is the landmark of Westfalenpark. A viewing platform gives a view over the Ruhr area.
new.tip: Entry to Westfalenpark is paid in season. Visit in clear weather for the long view.

new.title: Stroll Westfalenpark and its rose garden
new.desc: Westfalenpark is a 70-hectare park created for the 1959 Federal Garden Show, with rose gardens, a chair lift and open-air events. In autumn the Lichterfest fills it with lanterns.
new.tip: Evening light and the Lichterfest make it worth a second visit.

new.title: Visit the Reinoldikirche in the Old Town
new.desc: St. Reinold's is the oldest main church in Dortmund, with a late Romanesque nave and a Gothic choir. It stands on the medieval Hellweg trade route.
new.tip: Free to enter; the tower is lit at night.

new.title: See the Berswordt altar in St. Mary's church
new.desc: The Marienkirche is a Romanesque church from the 12th century that holds the 1420 Berswordt altarpiece by Conrad von Soest. It is among the oldest preserved churches in central Dortmund.
new.tip: Opening times are limited; check the parish website.

new.title: Admire the Goldaltar of St. Petri
new.desc: The Petrikirche houses the Goldene Wunder von Dortmund, a large Flemish Gothic altarpiece from about 1521 with some 633 figures.
new.tip: The altar's doors are opened at set times each day; check the parish page.

new.title: Climb to Hohensyburg and the Vincketurm
new.desc: The Hohensyburg ridge above the Ruhr and Lenne valleys has medieval castle ruins, the Vincketurm and the Kaiser-Wilhelm monument. A casino also sits on the hill.
new.tip: Walk up to the ruins for the view over the Hengstey and Harkort lakes.

new.title: Walk through the Rombergpark botanical garden
new.desc: The Rombergpark is a botanical garden and arboretum known for its rhododendron and magnolia collections. It borders the Zoo and the Phoenix area.
new.tip: Entry is free; visit in May for the rhododendron bloom.

new.title: Visit Zoo Dortmund
new.desc: Zoo Dortmund opened in 1953 and houses over 1,000 animals from more than 200 species. It is known for its South American animals.
new.tip: Combine with a walk in the neighbouring Rombergpark.

new.title: Learn about Pils at the Dortmund Brewery Museum
new.desc: The Brauerei-Museum tells the story of Dortmund as a beer city, with historic brewing equipment. The Hansa Pils dates back to 1902.
new.tip: Check opening hours (Thursday late opening until 20:00 was listed).

new.title: Drink Hövels Original at the Hausbrauerei
new.desc: Hövels Hausbrauerei at Hoher Wall serves its own beer and hearty German dishes. It is a classic Dortmund brewpub, open daily from 11:00 until late.
new.tip: Good for groups; try the house beer with a Schnitzel.

new.title: Order a Pils at Wenkers am Markt
new.desc: Wenkers am Markt is a brewery restaurant on the Markt in the Old Town, listed among the city's popular brewpubs. It serves local beer with regional dishes.
new.tip: Sit outside on the market square in summer.

new.title: Have breakfast at Kieztörtchen in the Kreuzviertel
new.desc: Kieztörtchen is a bakery-café in the Kreuzviertel, recommended by a local expert as a breakfast favourite. The district is one of the most popular for cafés and bars.
new.tip: Come before 11 for a quiet table; try a Törtchen with coffee.

new.title: Browse the Dortmund Christmas Market and giant tree
new.desc: The Dortmund Weihnachtsmarkt centres on a tree of about 45 metres made from some 1,700 spruces on Hansaplatz. It is among the largest Christmas markets in Germany.
new.tip: Go on a weekday evening to avoid the crowds.

new.title: Wander the Dortmund harbour and Speicherstraße
new.desc: Dortmund's canal harbour at the end of the Dortmund-Ems Canal is Europe's largest canal harbour. The old warehouses along Speicherstraße now hold offices and a few places to eat.
new.tip: Evenings give good photo light.

new.title: Catch a concert at the Konzerthaus Dortmund
new.desc: The Konzerthaus Dortmund opened in 2002 and hosts the Dortmund Philharmonic and international orchestras. It is known for its acoustics.
new.tip: Book tickets online ahead.

new.title: Catch an event at the Westfalenhallen
new.desc: The Westfalenhallen complex dates from 1925 and hosts concerts, fairs and sports events. It is a long-standing Dortmund event venue.
new.tip: Check the event calendar.

new.title: See working life at DASA Arbeitswelt Ausstellung
new.desc: DASA is a museum in Dortmund about work, with exhibits on technology and working conditions.
new.tip: Hands-on exhibits suit a rainy day; check admission hours.

new.title: Run or cycle in Hoeschpark
new.desc: Hoeschpark in the north-east of Dortmund is a large green space with a stadium and many sports facilities.
new.tip: A good place for a jog or a picnic.

new.title: Visit Schloss Bodelschwingh
new.desc: Schloss Bodelschwingh is a moated castle of the 16th century in the Dortmund district of Bodelschwingh, surrounded by a park.
new.tip: The grounds are open at set times.

new.title: See a show at the Opernhaus Dortmund
new.desc: The Dortmund Opera House on Platz von Leeds opened in 1966 and stages opera and ballet.
new.tip: Buy tickets in advance for popular performances.
new.q: Opernhaus Dortmund, Platz von Leeds, Dortmund

new.title: Go down the mine at the Deutsches Bergbau-Museum
new.desc: The Deutsches Bergbau-Museum is one of the world's largest mining museums, with a demonstration mine below the building. The Malakow tower on top gives a view over Bochum.
new.tip: Allow several hours; the lookout is reached by lift.
new.q: Deutsches Bergbau-Museum Bochum, Am Bergbaumuseum 28, Bochum

new.title: Watch Starlight Express in its own Bochum theatre
new.desc: Starlight Express by Andrew Lloyd Webber has run in Bochum since 1988 in a theatre built for it. It is one of the longest-running musicals in the world.
new.tip: Book ahead; shows run mostly Tuesday to Sunday.

new.title: Go out in the Bermuda3Eck
new.desc: The Bermuda3Eck is Bochum's pub and club district around Kortumstraße and Brüderstraße, with dozens of bars.
new.tip: Go after 9pm on weekends; start with a beer on Kortumstraße.

new.title: Eat a Dönninghaus Currywurst
new.desc: Dönninghaus is a cult currywurst address in the heart of Bochum's pub district, tied in tourism material to Herbert Grönemeyer's 'Currywurst' song.
new.tip: Open late; order it with fries.

new.title: See a show at the Zeiss Planetarium
new.desc: The Zeiss Planetarium Bochum is a planetarium in the Stadtpark with a Zeiss projector and a regular programme of astronomy shows.
new.tip: Check the show schedule online.
new.q: Zeiss Planetarium Bochum, Castroper Straße 67, Bochum

new.title: See the Jahrhunderthalle
new.desc: The Jahrhunderthalle is a steel hall from 1902 originally built for the Düsseldorf exhibition and moved to Bochum, now a venue for the Ruhrtriennale and concerts.
new.tip: Visit during an event or walk the Westpark around it.
new.q: Jahrhunderthalle Bochum, An der Jahrhunderthalle 1, Bochum

new.title: Walk the Westpark around the Jahrhunderthalle
new.desc: The Westpark Bochum is a park on the grounds of the former Bochumer Verein steelworks, with a pond and paths around the Jahrhunderthalle.
new.tip: Free to enter; combine with the Jahrhunderthalle.
new.q: Westpark Bochum, An der Jahrhunderthalle, Bochum

new.title: Walk or sail at Kemnader See
new.desc: Kemnader See is a reservoir on the Ruhr between Bochum and Witten with a walking and cycling loop, boat rentals and cafés.
new.tip: Rent a boat or cycle the Ruhrtalradweg.

new.title: Visit the moated Haus Kemnade
new.desc: Haus Kemnade is a medieval moated castle on the Ruhr by the Kemnader See, now a museum and restaurant.
new.tip: Combine with a walk around the lake.

new.title: See steam locomotives at the Eisenbahnmuseum Dahlhausen
new.desc: The Eisenbahnmuseum Bochum-Dahlhausen is a railway museum in a former locomotive depot with steam locomotives and carriages. It is open from March to mid-November.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Friday and Sunday in season.

new.title: Tour Zeche Hannover, the LWL mining museum
new.desc: Zeche Hannover in Hordel is an LWL industrial museum in a former coal mine, showing miners' daily life.
new.tip: Check the LWL site for tours and opening days.
new.q: LWL-Industriemuseum Zeche Hannover, Günnigfelder Straße 251, Bochum

new.title: Spend an hour at the Kunstmuseum Bochum
new.desc: The Kunstmuseum Bochum shows modern and contemporary art with a focus on the post-war period.
new.tip: Check opening days.

new.title: Walk to the Stiepeler Dorfkirche above the Ruhr
new.desc: Stiepel is a village district of Bochum with a Romanesque village church and the Kloster Stiepel above the Ruhr.
new.tip: Free to wander; the church has set opening hours.

new.title: Visit the Botanical Garden of Ruhr University
new.desc: The Botanischer Garten der Ruhr-Universität Bochum is a university garden with themed plant collections.
new.tip: Entry is free.

new.title: Catch a concert at Zeche Bochum
new.desc: Zeche Bochum is a music and event venue on Prinz-Regent-Straße with a rock and party programme.
new.tip: Check the programme online.

new.title: See a play at the Schauspielhaus Bochum
new.desc: The Schauspielhaus Bochum is one of Germany's best-known theatres, a post-war building on Königsallee.
new.tip: Book tickets in advance.

new.title: Hear the Bochum Symphony at the Musikforum
new.desc: The Anneliese Brost Musikforum Ruhr is the home of the Bochumer Symphoniker, with a concert hall built into a converted church.
new.tip: Check the season programme.
new.q: Anneliese Brost Musikforum Ruhr, Marienplatz 1, Bochum

new.title: Watch VfL Bochum at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion
new.desc: The Vonovia Ruhrstadion is the home ground of VfL Bochum, with a capacity of about 27,000 close to the city centre.
new.tip: Match tickets sell out fast.

new.title: Visit Schloss Strünkede in Herne
new.desc: Schloss Strünkede is a moated castle in Herne that houses the Emschertal-Museum, set in a park with a pond.
new.tip: Free to see from the park; the museum has set hours.

new.title: Ride at the Cranger Kirmes in Herne
new.desc: The Cranger Kirmes is one of Germany's largest fairground festivals, held on the Rhein-Herne Canal for eleven days each August. The 2026 edition runs 6-16 August.
new.tip: Weekdays are quieter; the opening day features a barrel tapping.

new.title: See a show at the Flottmann-Hallen in Herne
new.desc: The Flottmann-Hallen are a former machine factory in Herne converted into a cultural centre for theatre, concerts and art.
new.tip: Check the programme online.

new.title: Discover the LWL archaeology museum in Herne
new.desc: The LWL-Museum für Archäologie in Herne is the Westphalian archaeological museum with exhibits from the Stone Age to the Middle Ages.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays; check opening hours.
